records.context_summary: (e) Describe how a flame test is carried out.
creditworthy_points: INTERNAL SOURCE ANSWER (paraphrase before learner use): (e) Any two from: • use of (concentrated) hydrochloric acid (to clean) the wire / loop/ splint  • use of clean wire with solid sample / fresh splint / cotton / loop soaked in 2 (concentrated) solution  • blue / roaring / hot flame  Comments on question 4 The complete range of marks was seen in this planning question. The quality of responses was often centre-dependent. At some centres, candidates are getting more and more familiar with this type of question and their performance continues to improve. Better performing candidates at such centres were able to give well sequenced and logical descriptions of the investigation, in some instances, they were able to draw clear, well labelled diagrams, and were able to score up to full marks. Most candidates could make some progress and score in the range of 4 to 6 marks. At other centres, a significant number of candidates demonstrated that they did not have an idea of what a mortar and pestle is because they often went off-course by stating that they would put the mortar and pestle in a beaker and crush it. Other candidates demonstrated limited exposure to chromatography as an experimental technique altogether by going astray and describing biological tests such as iodine test/ benedict’s test, tests for reducing sugars etc. In general, other candidates used the wrong method such as fractional distillation or crystallisation. These methods showed a lack of knowledge and understanding of experimental techniques. Overall, the most common mark awarded was that of the crushing of the flower petals and the filtration of the mixture. Mark scheme Question Answer Mark 4 description on how to extract the colours present in purple flowers 6 • M1 crush the flower petals in a mortar with a pestle • M2 place (the crushed flower petals) in ethanol (and stir the mixture)  • M3 filter (to separate the solution from the rest of the mixture)  description on how to investigate the colours present in purple flowers • M4 draw a pencil line on a (rectangular) filter/chromatography paper / mark the centre of a (circular) filter/chromatography paper with a pencil  • M5 add pigment or sample spot on the line / add pigment or sample spot in the centre  • M6 insert paper into solvent such that the line is above solvent / add solvent to the spot using a dropper  • M7 allow for solvent to (dissolve pigment and) separate it into different colours  2 POSITIVE SUGGESTIONS TO TEACHERS To a large magnitude, the fashion in which learners responded to the questions in this paper, demonstrated that candidates have a limited conceptual understanding and exposure to practical experiences. Teachers are encouraged to use easily accessible and locally available / familiar materials to conduct practical activities in their classrooms. NSSCO Examiners Report 2022 99 Annexe A on Page 44 of the syllabus outlines the experimental contexts that guide the assessment objective C skills. At the end of each topic in the syllabus, there are also suggested practical activities. These should serve as a guide regarding the expectations of Paper 3. Lastly, it is important to reiterate that in terms of assessment objectives, there is a significant difference in the NSSCO Chemistry Paper 3 compared to the old curriculum NSSCO Physical Science Paper 3. On page 40 of the NSSCO Chemistry syllabus, the specification grid outlines that Paper 3 is only comprised of Assessment Objective C questions, the entire 40 marks, whilst the old curriculum NSSCO Physical Science Paper 3 used to be comprised of a combination of Assessment Objective A, B and C questions. This means that teachers need to put a great emphasis on assessment objective C and also make practical work an integral part of teaching and learning. NSSCO Examiners Report 2022 100

creditworthy_points: INTERNAL SOURCE ANSWER (paraphrase before learner use): (g) red (flame) 1 Total 10 Comments on question 4 Some excellent and fully correct answers to this quantitative planning question were seen. The quality of responses was often centre-dependent, with some centres doing exceptionally well. At some centres, candidates are getting more and more familiar with this type of question and their performance continues to improve. Better performing candidates at such centres were able to give well sequenced and logical descriptions of the investigation. In some instances, they were able to draw clear, well labelled diagrams, and were able to score up to full marks. Most candidates could make some progress and score in the range of 4 to 7 marks. At other centres, a significant number of candidates demonstrated that they were not familiar with rates (speeds) of reaction as specified in ANNEXE A: Assessment criteria for Paper 3, Alternative to Practical Paper on Page 44 of the NSSCO 6117 Chemistry syllabus. This question was based on experimental context 1 (b). A considerable number of candidates demonstrated that they did not understand the purpose of the A4 piece of paper with a cross marked on it as one of the materials provided on the list. They often went off-course by stating that they will either put the paper on the mouth of the conical flask; they will use the paper to plot a graph; or they will put the paper inside the conical flask to mix it with the contents of the conical flask. In general, a few candidates seemed to have related the A4 piece of paper with a cross marked on it to paper chromatography experiments because they gave responses which suggest that the cross on the paper needed to dissolve in a solvent to separate into different colours; or that a solvent needed to be poured onto the paper. This is probably because Question 4 of the 2022 Chemistry Paper 3 was based on an investigation on paper chromatography. Overall, the most common marks awarded were those of pouring the acid and the sodium thiosulfate into the conical flasks. Candidates are advised that ‘amount’ is not an acceptable term for volume (or mass). A minority of candidates did not attempt the question. NSSCO Examiners Report 2023 104 Question Answer Mark 4 Method 8 • M1 pour sodium thiosulfate into conical flask  • M2 place conical flask on the A4 paper (with cross marked on it  • M3 add a measured volume of hydrochloric to the conical flask with sodium thiosulfate  Measurements • M4 measure volume of hydrochloric acid using a measuring cylinder  • M5 measure time taken for cross to disappear using a stopwatch  • M6 repeat experiment with sodium thiosulfate of a different concentration  Variables to be controlled • M7 volume of hydrochloric acid  How the results would be used to reach a conclusion • M8 compare the time taken for the cross to disappear to the concentration of the thiosulfate to see if there is a pattern / relationship / trend  Total 8 POSITIVE SUGGESTIONS TO TEACHERS There is an improvement in the quality of responses by candidates in this cohort. Teachers are encouraged to keep exposing the candidates to practical experiences as a way to improve the performance in this paper for better. The emphasis is that the experimental contexts that guide the assessment objective C skills are stipulated as ANNEXE A on page 44 of the NSSCO 6117 Chemistry syllabus. In addition, there are also suggested practical activities at the end of each topic in the syllabus, which serve as a guide on the practical experiences to be exposed to candidates. These should serve as guidelines regarding the expectations of Paper 3. It is also important to highlight that in terms of assessment objectives; Paper 3 is set based on Assessment Objective C (see page 39 to 40 of the NSSCO 6117 Chemistry syllabus). records.context_summary: Use 6117/3/25 11 4 Zinc, iron and tin are metals. They react with dilute hydrochloric acid to form hydrogen gas. Plan an experiment to find the order of reactivity of these three metals. You are provided with: • samples of each metal • dilute hydrochloric acid • common laboratory apparatus. Describe and explain how you would carry out the experiment, including the apparatus you would use. • Make it clear how your experiment will be a fair test. • State the measurements you would take. • State how you will use your results to reach a conclusion.
creditworthy_points: M1 (1 mark): put each metal separately in contact with hydrochloric acid using a suitable reaction vessel.

M2–M3 (2 marks together): make a fair comparison using distinct controls from acid volume, acid concentration, acid temperature, metal surface area or form, and metal mass; the report caps this section at two marks from four valid control points.

M4–M5 (2 marks together): state a coherent pair of measurements. Accepted routes include timing from metal addition until reaction ends, measuring gas volume after a fixed interval, or comparing initial and peak temperatures.
M6 (1 mark): rank the metals from the chosen measure; shorter time, greater fixed-time gas volume, or greater temperature change indicates the more reactive metal, as applicable.
Apparatus earns credit only when its use in the method is stated; a bare list does not earn that credit.
examiner_findings: In planning answers, candidates named apparatus without saying what it was used for; a bare list did not earn the available credit.
